turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Describe a frontend feature you worked on. How did data move from a user action to the interface, and what did you implement?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I helped adjust spacing around the queue controls. I did not own the request layer and cannot explain its state transitions.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: I implemented all the request sequencing and the stale-response guard in the queue.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Walk me through a user-facing defect you investigated. What did you observe, and how did you decide what was causing it?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: I traced the production defect to an out-of-order response and verified the fix.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I cannot attribute that investigation to myself. That section of the recording is unclear, and I do not remember carrying out a diagnosis.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How did you check the change and decide it was ready for release?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I ran the existing test command and it passed. I did not inspect its assertions or know whether it covered this change.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What accessibility work or checks did you perform on this interface?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I personally used Tab to move through the queue buttons. After closing the help panel with Escape, I checked that focus returned to its trigger button. I did not test a screen reader.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Looking back, what were the limits of your ownership or evidence, and what would you investigate or ask for help with next?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The two unattributed statements should not be treated as mine without confirming the speaker. My checks were limited to the actions I described.
